The perovskite precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L using PbI2 and MAI dissolved in a mixed DMF/DMSO solvent. A combination of Me-4PACz (0.198 mg/mL) and DMACPA (0.132 mg/mL) as SAMs were introduced to enhance interfacial properties and improve device performance. The addition of MACl (14.6 mg/mL) and PEAI (0.517 mg/mL) were instrumental in fine-tuning the perovskite film's optical properties. Employing a staged spin protocol, the film underwent 1000 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 35 s, enhancing film morphology. At the last 15 s of the second step, 200 µL anisole was dropped as antisolvent. By subjecting the film to 110 °C for 15 min, the perovskite lattice attained its ideal orientation. The passivator PEACl (1.4 mg/mL) was introduced into the system to improve material properties. The passivation solution was dynamically spin-coated on the annealed perovskite film at 5200.0 rpm for 30.0 s. The passivator volume of 120.0 µL was dropped at 7.0 s during spin-coating. The passivation layer was thermally treated at 100.0 °C for 3.0 min to improve its properties. Spectral analysis indicates that, upon the onset of annealing, the film reaches the explosive nucleation point at 3.8 seconds, at which the photoluminescence (PL) intensity attains its maximum. Following this peak, the PL intensity decreases to 30% of its maximum value, with an average decay slope of 1.990833333.
